newsitem.title: USA: NASA orders extra spacewalk to make Hubble repairs.
newsitem.headline: NASA orders extra spacewalk to make Hubble repairs.

text.p: NASA officials said on Sunday they expected to order an extra spacewalk from shuttle Discovery to make repairs to the Hubble Space Telescope's torn and tattered exterior.

The astronauts were to make a fourth spacewalk on Sunday night to complete their planned servicing tasks and begin repairs to rips and tears in the silvery foil covering much of the telescope exterior. A fifth spacewalk would be needed to complete the work.
NASA managers, meeting on Sunday morning, were expected to schedule the extra spacewalk for Monday night and delay the release of the telescope until Tuesday.
Scientists were concerned the damaged foil, which protects the telescope from the harsh environment of space, could peel off and contaminate the telescope's delicate optics.
Engineers and astronauts on the ground were devising a plan to tie patches over four areas of the telescope's exterior, including one long rip in the foil close to the top of the telescope.
Earlier, Mark Lee and Steve Smith, making the third spacewalk of the mission, took a close-up look at some of the damage and upgraded three ageing telescope components.
